✅ In confirmation rule

Metrics included in distress confirmation rule

A confirmed distress signal requires ≥2 of these metrics at Stress+ simultaneously
MetricCohen d95% CIORpRationale
leverage+1.76—5.73<0.05Large effect — Altman (1968) benchmark. Zero false positives.
interest_coverage+1.68—3.09<0.05Large effect — only metric with d>1.5 AND zero false positives across 31 controls.
free_cash_flow+0.80———Medium-large effect. Reliable FCF signal.
quick_ratio+0.49———Retained — liquidity signal. Sector-adjusted thresholds.
ebitda_margin+0.15———Retained — trend signal across all sectors.
maturity_coverage+0.12———Structural near-term liquidity signal.
(13 others)various———Retained pending larger sample (n≥50 recommended for threshold recalibration).
❌ Excluded from confirmation rule

Metrics excluded from distress confirmation rule

Displayed in company monitor but do not count toward the ≥2-metric confirmation threshold
MetricCohen d95% CIORpRationale
current_ratio−0.05—0.980.92Statistically inert — fires equally on healthy and distressed. Altman (1968) found current ratio to be a weak standalone predictor.
debt_to_equity+1.06—2.04<0.01Capital structure artifact — 66 Critical-quarters on 31 healthy controls vs 18 on 30 distressed. Fires on buyback-heavy IG companies with negative book equity.
rcf_net_debt+1.30—2.85<0.01Low sensitivity — Stress+ in only 50% of distressed at first signal. Dividend seasonality causes RCF<0 in payout quarters for healthy IG companies.
Statistical benchmarks: Cohen (1988) d guidelines: 0.2=small, 0.5=medium, 0.8=large. Only leverage and interest_coverage reach Altman (1968) benchmark separation (d>1.2) with CI lower bound above 0.8. Reference: Altman, E.I. (1968). Journal of Finance, 23(4), 589–609. All findings exploratory — n=30 distressed cases, 33 healthy controls.
